AB 1026.quote: it is largely duplicative of existing efforts and risks disrupting the current public decision-making processes at the CPUC
AB 1026.reason: AB 50 and SB 410 (2023) already required the CPUC to set connection and energization targets, which it did in September 2024; standardized procedures here are largely duplicative, risk disrupting the CPUC's public process, and complicate the customer application process.

AB 1032.quote: passing additional policies that would lead to further premium increases would be irresponsible
AB 1032.reason: Commercial plan enrollees already have behavioral health coverage regardless of wildfire emergencies, and the bill's broad carve-out from utilization review and out-of-network limits would add cost — irresponsible when consumers face double-digit premium increases nationwide.

AB 1039.quote: imposing a new statewide requirement would severely limit the state's oversight and protection of public funds
AB 1039.reason: Wants to lower financial barriers for nonprofits and tribes, but a statewide advance-payment mandate would limit the state's oversight and protection of public funds; AB 590 (2023) and AB 3017 (2024) already let agencies make advance payments, and agencies need discretion to weigh the risk of each request.

AB 1042.quote: this bill would create an unfunded grant program and, therefore, should be considered as part of the annual budget process
AB 1042.reason: Appreciates protecting honeybees, but a Managed Honeybee Health Program would be an unfunded grant program and should be considered in the annual budget process.

AB 1049.quote: the changes proposed by this bill would create a significant inconsistency between the federally funded CalFresh program and the state-funded CFAP program
AB 1049.reason: Applauds removing barriers to food assistance, but exempting CFAP from sponsor deeming would split it from CalFresh, which uses the same application and the same deeming rules, creating discrepancies the current federal administration could weaponize. Existing deeming exemptions already serve the bill's intent, and he directed the department to publicize them.

AB 1054.quote: Both the design and establishment of a DROP are more appropriately handled through the collective bargaining process
AB 1054.reason: A voluntary DROP could help staffing, but it may create significant long-term fiscal and administrative pressure by changing employee tenures and retirement costs, and both the design and creation of a DROP belong in collective bargaining.

AB 1064.quote: AB 1064 imposes such broad restrictions on the use of conversational AI tools that it may unintentionally lead to a total ban on the use of these products by minors
AB 1064.reason: He signed SB 243 requiring chatbot platforms to detect and respond to self-harm signals, tell minors they are talking to AI, and block sexual content; this bill's restrictions are so broad they could effectively ban conversational AI for minors, and young people need to learn to use and evaluate these tools. He committed to building on SB 243 next year.

AB 1074.quote: this bill results in ongoing costs that were not accounted for in the 2025 Budget Act
AB 1074.reason: Supports removing barriers in CalWORKs Family Reunification, but the expanded cash aid period and eligibility changes create ongoing costs that were not accounted for in the 2025 Budget Act.

AB 1089.quote: this bill goes too far in authorizing the blanket removal of these trees near single-family homes
AB 1089.reason: The 2023 Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act already balances Mojave development with species protection; authorizing blanket removal of trees near single-family homes goes too far and would undermine those protections while making permitting more complex and slower.

AB 1099.quote: this bill would create significant, ongoing General Fund cost pressures to fund local assistance costs annually
AB 1099.reason: Shares the goal of timely regional center access for foster youth, but the mandated case-conference and assessment timelines would create significant ongoing General Fund costs, and the Department of Developmental Services is already standardizing intake across the 21 regional centers under SB 138.

AB 1116.quote: this bill would result in one-time and ongoing costs in the millions of dollars not included in the 2026 Budget Act
AB 1116.reason: Supports removing barriers to voter registration, but building online registration for people without a California driver's license or ID would cost millions of dollars in one-time and ongoing spending that is not in the 2026 Budget Act.

AB 1136.quote: The bill duplicates existing discrimination protections and is inconsistent with other leave frameworks in state law
AB 1136.reason: Commends the intent, but the leave and reinstatement rules duplicate existing discrimination protections, conflict with other state leave frameworks, and the 12-month rehire window is impractical (and interferes with school district rehire protections); enforcement would force the Labor Commissioner into costly civil actions exceeding $10 million a year.

AB 1143.quote: rather than providing a coordinated approach, these measures are in conflict with one another, tasking different state entities with similar objectives
AB 1143.reason: California already runs the Wildfire Mitigation Program, a statewide home-hardening playbook, and CDI's 'Safer from Wildfires' discount framework; this year's competing bills task different agencies with similar goals, producing conflicting outcomes and confusion for consumers, insurers, and local governments. He asked the Legislature to come back with one coordinated approach.

AB 1165.quote: this bill layers a new finance-planning and reporting mandate onto existing work at a time when the state should be focused on delivering programs and measuring results
AB 1165.reason: Supports the goal of ending homelessness, but says the bill piles another finance-planning and reporting mandate onto work already underway and bases statewide funding estimates on static conditions even as housing costs, production, and needs change. New mandates should clear a high bar and add something beyond existing efforts.

AB 1200.quote: The exercises envisioned in this bill are overly broad and lack clarity
AB 1200.reason: Cal OES already runs targeted, multi-jurisdictional tabletop exercises aligned with existing plans; the mandated exercises here are overly broad and unclear, could undermine current preparedness efforts, and would add millions of dollars in ongoing costs.

AB 1210.quote: the practical implications of this bill would result in significant, ongoing costs to the state with limited benefit to public safety
AB 1210.reason: Release dates shift with credits and sentencing changes, so a 90-day notice would trigger repeated recurring notifications to counties for limited public safety benefit, with significant General Fund impacts not in the 2025 Budget Act.

AB 1224.quote: this bill would allow individuals to serve our highest-need students for as much as a third of a school year without minimally required training
AB 1224.reason: Substitutes disproportionately serve students with disabilities, English learners, and low-income students; doubling or tripling the caps to 60 days without mandating participation in mentorship and training would let people serve high-need students for a third of the year unprepared.

AB 1225.quote: this bill would be duplicative of the Department's existing Accessibility Division
AB 1225.reason: Duplicative of the department's existing Accessibility Division, which has completed hundreds of barrier-removal and accessible trail projects under a court-approved consent decree timeline.

AB 1273.quote: this bill's requirements on the CPUC’s public decision-making processes risk delaying action on critical issues
AB 1273.reason: The CPUC is already bound by the Bagley-Keene Open Meeting Act and its own Rules of Practice and Procedure, which give the public ample opportunity to comment; constraining how it uses a consent agenda risks delaying action on critical issues.

AB 1309.quote: Establishing a statutory salary floor for employees of a single department undermines this process
AB 1309.reason: Would create significant state cost pressure and circumvent collective bargaining: state salaries and benefits should be set at the table, and a statutory salary floor for one department undermines that process to the detriment of the state and other bargaining units.

AB 1324.quote: this bill creates significant, ongoing cost pressures not accounted for in the 2025 Budget Act
AB 1324.reason: Supports expanding CalWORKs eligibility for working families in poverty, but the bill creates significant ongoing cost pressures not accounted for in the 2025 Budget Act.

AB 1326.quote: This bill creates a sweeping new policy with numerous exceptions, and may create confusion
AB 1326.reason: Not convinced it is necessary: existing law already appears to let people mask for health reasons in most public situations, and this sweeping new policy with numerous exceptions could create confusion about existing state and federal protections.

AB 1328.quote: mandating rate increases for ground ambulance services could create inappropriate incentives to utilize ambulance transport over other more appropriate and available modes
AB 1328.reason: Supports access to nonemergency medical transportation, but pegging rates to 80% of the Medicare ambulance fee schedule would create incentives to use ambulances instead of cheaper, more appropriate modes, and would cost the General Fund tens of millions of dollars a year.

AB 1329.quote: AB 1329 does not contain the comprehensive reforms necessary to save SIBTF
AB 1329.reason: The Subsequent Injury Benefit Trust Fund desperately needs reform — assessments could go from $372 million to $1.5 billion by 2029-30 and claims face ten-year delays — but this bill is not comprehensive enough and some changes move it the wrong way, such as counting 'activities of daily living,' which would increase claims. He directed comprehensive reform in the 2026-27 budget.

AB 1332.quote: the costs of administering this program far outweigh the possible benefits to patients
AB 1332.reason: Supports patient access, but direct shipping would force the Department of Cannabis Control to revamp the track-and-trace system, the product restrictions are unclear, narrow, or unworkable, and with only two businesses eligible the administrative cost far outweighs the benefit.

AB 1336.quote: The workers' compensation system is not equipped to make determinations about employers' compliance with Cal/OSHA standards
AB 1336.reason: He vetoed a nearly identical bill last year: heat illness prevention is Cal/OSHA's jurisdiction, and the workers' compensation system is not equipped to decide whether an employer met Cal/OSHA standards, so a presumption would cause delays and dilute the benefit. Cal/OSHA has since opened 250+ proactive inspections and addressed heat at 395 worksites.

AB 1348.quote: AB 1348 does not include sufficient safeguards to ensure that students who miss school due to immigration enforcement activities will receive alternative instructional opportunities
AB 1348.reason: Districts can already recover attendance through recovery and independent study programs, and the bill lacks safeguards that students missing school over immigration enforcement get alternative instruction; it also adds cost pressure where funding already uses a three-year rolling attendance average as a buffer.

AB 1373.quote: The Board's certification process already includes opportunities for input by members of the public and Board members
AB 1373.reason: Unnecessary: the water board's certification process already allows public and board-member input, including reconsideration of decisions delegated to staff. He directed the board to look for efficiencies consistent with the bill's intent.

AB 1378.quote: It is unclear whether the types of agreements proposed by this bill can be used to access federal funds
AB 1378.reason: Recognizes the disparities tribal families face, but the proposed tribal agreements have significant fiscal, legal, and programmatic problems — it is unclear they can be used to access federal Family First funds — and the administration's alternative approach was not accepted, leaving the bill deeply flawed.

AB 1383.quote: This measure would partially reverse some of PEPRA's reforms and significantly increase state and local government costs
AB 1383.reason: Would partially roll back PEPRA and significantly raise state and local costs, and widening the benefit gap between safety and non-safety members invites further changes that add risk to the retirement system. PEPRA was born of a crisis he does not want to repeat.

AB 1400.quote: Given these significant changes, a pause should be maintained to understand their full impact before additional authorities are granted
AB 1400.reason: He vetoed a nearly identical bill last year for the same two reasons: $60 million a year through 2028-29 already funds BSN partnerships with UC, CSU, and nonprofits, and both CCC and CSU recently gained authority to offer programs outside their traditional roles, so a pause is needed to see the impact before granting more.

AB 1408.quote: this bill risks constraining energy resource procurement and interconnection options, likely increasing customer electric costs
AB 1408.reason: Grid planning across CAISO, the Energy Commission, and the CPUC is a highly technical, constantly refined system; mandating surplus-interconnection rules risks constraining procurement and interconnection options, raising customer costs and undermining reliability.

AB 1430.quote: raising these fees on Californians will disincentivize efforts to think innovatively about how to deliver recording services at a lower cost
AB 1430.reason: Recorder offices matter to homeowners, but raising recording and indexing fees would disincentivize counties from finding cheaper, faster, better ways to deliver recording services; he urged achieving the goal without relying solely on fee increases.

AB 15.quote: Diverting resources from active cases could lead to more unsolved crimes, not fewer
AB 15.reason: Supports solving cold cases, but they usually reflect a lack of evidence rather than diligence; meeting the mandated review timelines would force agencies to hire or pull investigators off active homicides, which could produce more unsolved crimes, not fewer.

AB 1537.quote: establishing a default prohibition regarding the secondary employment law enforcement officers choose to do in their free time is a step too far
AB 1537.reason: Agrees that federal immigration raids have been abusive and calls on Congress to act, but says a blanket ban on the secondary jobs officers take in their free time is a step too far: officers are already bound by conduct standards and can have their peace officer status suspended or revoked.

AB 1542.quote: a categorical ban on sharing that information is a step too far
AB 1542.reason: Wants sensitive personal information protected, but an outright ban on selling or sharing it is a step too far because consumers already have the right to limit that sharing and may be worse off if removed from the decision entirely; applying it to all CCPA businesses also brings significant unbudgeted implementation and enforcement costs.

AB 1547.quote: it requires significant General Fund resources that are not included in the 2026 Budget Act
AB 1547.reason: Requires significant General Fund resources not in the 2026 Budget Act, and AB 2357 (2024) already created the UC Kern County Medical Education Endowment Fund whose money may be used for exactly this feasibility study.

AB 1562.quote: this bill could inadvertently redirect resources away from local election officials administering free and fair elections
AB 1562.reason: Appreciates the civic-engagement goal, but a random-selection system for precinct board members would take a tremendous amount of county staff and money, and with election systems under attack it could pull resources away from running free and fair elections.

AB 1567.quote: local governments could receive credit toward their lower-income housing obligations for facilities unaffordable to lower-income residents
AB 1567.reason: Supports senior and supportive housing, but the bill lets cities count congregate and residential care units toward any income category without showing the facilities serve households at that level, so local governments could claim credit for lower-income obligations they are not meeting. It also never explains how to count beds and units or prevent duplicative credit.

AB 1591.reason: Duplicates existing work: HCAI already runs workforce pathway programs that include podiatric medicine, and the two special funds the bill points to are already committed elsewhere, with no new money in this year's budget.

AB 1595.quote: the bill would add to the trial courts' caseload, potentially causing court backlogs and creating pressure on the General Fund
AB 1595.reason: Expanded habeas pleading standards would add workload for DOJ, corrections, state hospitals, public defenders, and district attorneys, and add to trial court caseloads, risking backlogs and General Fund pressure.

AB 1602.quote: this bill would create a new, unfunded grant program
AB 1602.reason: Shares the goal of helping foster youth through disasters, but this creates a new unfunded grant program; he vetoed an identical bill last year for the same reason — no identified funding source means ongoing General Fund pressure — and that has not changed.

AB 1608.quote: The Office should continue working with the appropriate state agencies to address its operational needs through existing processes rather than receive broad, permanent exemptions
AB 1608.reason: The office has already been strengthened this year (whistleblower protections, sensitive investigative records) and is due more IT delegation authority; it should meet its operational needs through existing state processes rather than receive broad, permanent exemptions from statewide administrative safeguards.

AB 1647.quote: By its own terms, the bill is "declaratory of existing law" and therefore unnecessary
AB 1647.reason: Unnecessary: the bill says it does not restrict, expand, alter, or modify the California Supreme Court decisions that have governed this issue for more than 40 years and is, by its own terms, declaratory of existing law.

AB 1666.quote: The program proposed in this measure would require additional resources not included in this year's budget
AB 1666.reason: Thanks the author and points to $50 million already steered from the Climate Bond to large-scale biomass facilities, but the new grant program would need money not in this year's budget, and he says the state must stay disciplined on bills with significant fiscal implications outside the budget.

AB 1722.quote: This bill duplicates these protections while creating confusion about the applicable standard for invoking this type of defense
AB 1722.reason: California law already shields someone who takes a listed species in self-defense or defense of another from penalties; the bill duplicates that protection while creating confusion about the standard for invoking the defense.

AB 1729.quote: This measure, by limiting departmental flexibility and encouraging telework to be the default work arrangement, takes the state's telework policy in the wrong direction
AB 1729.reason: Believes in-person collaboration matters and notes existing policy already lets departments seek case-by-case exemptions; requiring written justifications and decennial telework updates limits departmental flexibility and pushes telework toward being the default, the wrong direction.

AB 1761.quote: this legislation will result in improper dissemination of market-sensitive information and benefit a limited subset of market participants
AB 1761.reason: Concerned the bill would lead to improper dissemination of market-sensitive information benefiting a limited subset of market participants, when the CPUC already has approved confidentiality procedures and a process developed with load-serving entities to access the same data with proper guardrails.

AB 1813.quote: It would effectively require an administratively set price for the generation of power that exceeds the value that generation provides to the grid
AB 1813.reason: Calls the bill structurally flawed: it would effectively set an administratively fixed price for community solar above the value that power delivers to the grid, pushing rates up (the Public Advocates Office estimates up to $1.5 billion a year for ratepayers) without adding reliable capacity when the grid needs it.

AB 1832.quote: this bill would result in millions of dollars in ongoing costs for Cal OES to implement, as well as tens of millions of dollars in ongoing cost pressures outside of the budget
AB 1832.reason: Appreciates the goal of a funding mechanism for 211 providers, but the fund would mean millions of dollars in ongoing Cal OES implementation costs plus tens of millions more in ongoing cost pressure outside the budget.

AB 1881.quote: this legislation's proposed framework could have far-reaching impacts on the basic operations of state government and the management of state property, and this uncertainty calls for further discussion and review
AB 1881.reason: Sympathetic to protecting tribal religious practice on state land, but the framework could reach far into basic state operations and property management; that uncertainty calls for more discussion and review, and he encourages the author to keep refining the concepts with state agencies.

AB 1882.quote: instead enacts a new, complex, and unfunded hospital reimbursement program
AB 1882.reason: This budget already put $90 million (expandable by $50 million) into distressed hospitals, $250 million into public hospitals, and $10 million into a new HCAI healthcare stability unit; this bill draws on none of that and instead creates a new, complex, unfunded reimbursement program with costly reporting duties.

AB 1889.quote: Tying a protective order to the date of release requires information that will simply not be available to the court
AB 1889.reason: Cannot be implemented reliably: release dates shift with workgroup assignments, credit earnings and losses, and sentencing changes, all unknowable at sentencing when the court would issue the order, so law enforcement systems would hold inaccurate information and confuse officers and victims alike.

AB 1891.quote: this bill limits CAL FIRE's ability to prioritize limited state resources toward the projects and communities facing the greatest wildfire risks
AB 1891.reason: Prescribed burning has nearly doubled since 2021 to about 200,000 acres a year, and he shares the goal of going faster, but earmarking a set share of CAL FIRE grant money would stop the department from steering limited resources to the projects and communities at greatest wildfire risk. Funding choices like this belong in the budget.

AB 1894.quote: I am concerned by this bill's "one-size-fits-all" approach prohibiting the denial of local water deliveries
AB 1894.reason: Since golden mussels were detected in October 2024 the administration has worked with infested and uninfested water managers on prevention and containment; a one-size-fits-all bar on denying water deliveries could have serious unintended consequences as the mussel threat evolves.

AB 1896.quote: establishing a default employment prohibition for any individual engaged in enforcing federal civil immigration laws is a step too far
AB 1896.reason: Same theme as AB 1537: a default bar on hiring anyone who took part in federal immigration enforcement is a step too far, would discourage qualified people from federal service, and is unnecessary because state and local hiring already screens personal conduct with accountability built in.

AB 1940.quote: The approach taken by this measure may have the unintended consequence of authorizing a FEHA lawsuit for all adverse employment decisions made against a very large segment of the working population
AB 1940.reason: Supports protecting women going through menopause and notes his budget added menopause drug coverage, screening, and clinician training, but says menopause-related conditions that rise to a disability are already covered by FEHA and this approach could open FEHA lawsuits over a huge share of the workforce, with substantial General Fund costs.

AB 1949.quote: I do not believe it is appropriate to legislate additional visit requirements outside the annual budget process due to its impact on utilization and costs
AB 1949.reason: Medi-Cal already covers two acupuncture visits a month and the department can update coverage administratively to match the standard of care; legislating additional visit levels outside the annual budget process drives utilization and cost, so it belongs in the budget.

AB 1967.quote: this bill's proposed changes to the eligibility standards for reentry into foster care would actually exacerbate, rather than mitigate, these delays
AB 1967.reason: Laudable intent, but the new reentry standards would make delays worse: they make eligibility harder to determine and allow reentry only for youth receiving no support at all, a higher bar than today that would turn away young people who get very little support and still need foster care.

AB 1997.quote: this bill creates further statutory ambiguity by failing to clarify how its deadline applies to subsequent project approvals that rely on a program, master, or staged EIR
AB 1997.reason: Supports faster approvals for deeply affordable housing, but the bill is unclear about how its 30-day clock applies when a project relies on a program, master, or staged EIR that still needs project-specific review. Given the narrow set of projects covered, that ambiguity risks projects being denied or deemed approved under uncertain rules.

AB 2012.quote: This bill would change longstanding permitting and escort requirements before the workgroup it creates has evaluated whether and how those requirements can safely be revised
AB 2012.reason: Supports lowering housing construction costs, but oversized loads require route-specific review of lane widths, turning radii, clearances, work zones, and traffic. The bill changes longstanding permitting and escort rules before the very workgroup it creates has evaluated whether they can safely be revised.

AB 2066.quote: it would have set a dangerous precedent for condition-specific special enrollment periods and created substantial instability in the individual health insurance market
AB 2066.reason: He vetoed a substantially similar bill last year because condition-specific special enrollment periods set a dangerous precedent and create instability in the individual health insurance market, and those concerns remain as consumers face uncertainty over coverage affordability.

AB 2081.quote: this bill would significantly and immediately increase program costs by hundreds of millions of dollars
AB 2081.reason: Adding 5,000 HCBA waiver slots would immediately raise program costs by hundreds of millions of dollars; the 2026 budget already includes $3 million for DHCS to clear the waiver waitlist, and any larger expansion belongs in the budget process.

AB 2122.quote: By eliminating misdemeanor liability and arrest authority for failures to appear, this bill could cause additional delays in the court processing of unsafe driving violations
AB 2122.reason: He has repealed or reduced dozens of fines and fees and discharged nearly $7 billion in debt, but this bill does not balance relief with public safety: eliminating misdemeanor liability and arrest authority for failure to appear on traffic infractions would slow court processing and delay notice to DMV — with a State Auditor review of exactly that process still pending.

AB 2124.quote: the resources required to implement this bill were not considered in the context of this year's budget agreement
AB 2124.reason: Legislative professional staff and the Legislative Analyst's Office already analyze pending bills, including ratepayer impacts, so a new Council on Science and Technology review program is redundant — and its cost was not considered in this year's budget agreement.

AB 2142.quote: this bill creates hundreds of millions of dollars in additional cost pressures and should be considered within the broader context of the annual state budget process
AB 2142.reason: Supports keeping 'short-term' employees from being hired year after year without permanent status, but the statutory thresholds, service-day calculations, and legal standard would be confusing to implement, and the bill creates hundreds of millions of dollars in cost pressure that belongs in the budget process.

AB 2164.quote: extradition is an exclusively executive function. When discretionary, that discretion is appropriately placed with the Governor
AB 2164.reason: Proud of the state's shield laws protecting reproductive care, but extradition is an exclusively executive function and its discretion belongs with the Governor; he is troubled by an outgoing administration stripping that authority from an incoming governor based on shared policy preferences.

AB 2166.quote: this novel program is estimated to require hundreds of millions of dollars in initial capitalization, funding that was not included in the state budget
AB 2166.reason: Supports innovative financing to cut housing costs, but this novel surety-bond backstop is estimated to need hundreds of millions of dollars in initial capitalization that is not in the budget; a proposal of that scale should be evaluated in the budget process alongside its risk protections and administration.

AB 2186.quote: because the full scope of the proposed tax exclusion is unknown, fiscal caution is warranted
AB 2186.reason: Proud of last year's Bureau for Descendants of American Slavery, but says the scope of the proposed tax exclusion is unknown and its federal-law prong could be read broadly, creating fiscal uncertainty; a change with potentially significant General Fund effects should go through the budget process.

AB 220.quote: this bill is no longer necessary
AB 220.reason: No longer necessary: Medi-Cal managed care plans are already required to apply subacute medical-necessity criteria in line with Medi-Cal policy, and in response to this bill the department published clarifying guidance in June without limiting utilization management or adding General Fund costs.

AB 2218.quote: adding new layers of process to duplicate work that my Administration already prioritizes
AB 2218.reason: Says his administration already goes beyond existing law on government-to-government work with tribes (a DWR tribal advisory committee, Tribal Beneficial Uses in water planning) and this bill would add duplicative layers of process with unclear implementation, slowing the state's work to secure water supplies under climate change.

AB 2230.quote: this bill places an undue burden on providers to validate the legality of the officer's action or verify specific legal documents
AB 2230.reason: Sympathetic to the fear immigration enforcement has created for child care providers (and points to AB 495 last year), but barring employees from ever giving voluntary consent puts an undue burden on providers to verify an officer's legal authority mid-incident, and could hinder legitimate licensing investigations and law enforcement visits unrelated to immigration.

AB 2247.quote: This measure is duplicative of those efforts and creates a new, unfunded grant program not included in the 2026 Budget Act
AB 2247.reason: Supports help for youth survivors of gun violence and points to the $12.5 million budget increase for Trauma Recovery Centers, but this measure duplicates that work and creates a new unfunded grant program that is not in the 2026 Budget Act.

AB 2253.quote: expanding these documentation requirements will unduly burden manufacturers and suppliers already facing economic headwinds caused by federal tariff and trade policy actions
AB 2253.reason: Wants recycled-content marketing claims to be accurate, but expanding the documentation rules to every product making such a claim would unduly burden manufacturers already squeezed by federal tariff and trade policy, adding complex compliance costs with little benefit to consumers.

AB 2282.quote: This bill would undermine patient safety by allowing the operation of an emergency department that lacks the statutorily required medical infrastructure of a GACH
AB 2282.reason: Shares the goal of rural emergency access, but freestanding emergency departments have never legally operated in California — state law requires the emergency department to sit inside the hospital. A unit without a general acute care hospital's infrastructure undermines patient safety and adds transfer risks and delays when minutes count.

AB 2301.quote: it is neither necessary nor appropriate to authorize an additional pilot or create an exception to the framework
AB 2301.reason: He signed SB 960 and AB 2694 creating a statewide community college bachelor's framework covering all programs that meet criteria like workforce demand, so a separate 10-district nursing pilot is neither necessary nor appropriate; plus $60 million a year through 2028-29 already funds nursing infrastructure grants and BSN partnerships.

AB 2314.quote: allowing an APP contractor to submit a VTT request at any time during the fiscal year conflicts with CDSS' existing statutory authority to set timelines
AB 2314.reason: Wants reliable childcare for families, but letting alternative payment contractors request a temporary fund transfer at any point in the fiscal year conflicts with the department's statutory authority to set timelines, puts annual fiscal reports and audits at risk, and the permissive language on moving funds out of a county clashes with the child care funding deal negotiated in the 2026 budget.

AB 2337.quote: The existing definition of serious misconduct therefore already encompasses the use of peace officer authority to commit theft
AB 2337.reason: Duplicative: 'serious misconduct' already includes abuse of power, dishonesty, and egregious violations of law, which covers theft under color of authority. Naming one more example is unnecessary and could imply other unspecified violations are not actionable.

AB 2343.quote: this bill is duplicative of existing efforts
AB 2343.reason: Duplicative: California launched the free, confidential Treatment Atlas in 2023 to help people find and compare addiction treatment, and the 2026 budget funds it through September 30, 2027, so a new consumer platform is unnecessary.

AB 2349.quote: the proposed program requires significant resources not included in this year's budget
AB 2349.reason: Shares the goal of expanding emergency air monitoring, but the expanded incident monitoring program requires significant resources that were not included in this year's budget.

AB 2367.quote: this measure would create substantial operational and technological burdens for affected departments by requiring the creation of more complex reporting structures than currently exist
AB 2367.reason: Sympathetic to giving the public more information on hiring and retention at state-run health facilities, but the measure would force four departments to build more complex reporting structures than they have today, costing millions of dollars in new General Fund spending.

AB 2369.quote: This bill would predetermine the treatment of these energy-only resources before that essential work is complete
AB 2369.reason: Premature: CAISO is studying energy-only resources in the 2026-2027 transmission planning process with results due November 2026, and those results will shape the CPUC's new Reliable and Clean Power Procurement Program. This bill would predetermine how energy-only resources are treated before that work finishes.

AB 239.quote: This bill would duplicate longstanding work already underway, create additional costs and reporting requirements, and limit the flexibility
AB 239.reason: California already has the structure: after the Eaton and Palisades Fires, HCD and Cal OES created a Housing Task Force inside the Joint Field Office that convenes state, federal, and local partners, launched resiliency centers, and held rebuild workshops. The bill would duplicate that, add costs and reporting, and limit flexibility that disaster response depends on.

AB 2395.quote: the new complaint resolution process envisioned by this bill would require administrators to review and potentially overturn their own decisions
AB 2395.reason: Supports access to the child support debt reduction program, but mandating highly specific statewide forms adds complexity for improvements the department can make administratively under existing authority, and the new complaint process would have administrators review and possibly overturn their own decisions — an inherent conflict of interest.

AB 2402.quote: I do not believe it is in the best interest of Californians to remove this cap, which could price consumers out of these clubs altogether
AB 2402.reason: Health studio contract rules exist to shield consumers from excessive fees and predatory sales, and the $4,400 cap limits their exposure to large future payment obligations; removing it could price consumers out of these clubs altogether.

AB 2439.quote: The bill neither defines nor limits those costs. This broad standard could create uncertainty, invite disputes and litigation
AB 2439.reason: Supports protecting homeowners from improper collection practices, but the bill makes associations liable for undefined 'any costs,' exposes board members personally to a $1,000 penalty without explaining how that works as membership changes, and mandates certified mail with return receipts — uncertainty, litigation risk, and administrative costs passed to homeowners.

AB 2465.quote: this bill's requirements are unclear and expand beyond the stated intent
AB 2465.reason: Shares the goal of keeping state dollars away from private prisons and immigration enforcement contractors, but says the bill's requirements are unclear and sweep beyond that intent, potentially cutting off businesses that provide ordinary goods and services to agencies with much wider duties and interfering with lawful state programs and economic development.

AB 2494.quote: By narrowing the management of these forests to a limited set of public benefits, this bill risks the State's ability to fully demonstrate the best science-based practices
AB 2494.reason: The Demonstration State Forests have served 80 years as living laboratories; narrowing their management to a limited set of public benefits risks the state's ability to demonstrate the best science-based practices and removes flexibility needed as the climate changes.

AB 2502.quote: this bill as drafted introduces significant uncertainties into DUI law, which could have the unintended consequence of making it more difficult to hold dangerous drivers accountable
AB 2502.reason: Agrees drivers should not escape DUI responsibility by engaging driver-assist technology, but the bill's undefined terms (like 'driver support features') inject uncertainty into DUI law and could force officers, prosecutors, and courts to litigate a car's software before deciding whether an impaired person was driving. The incident behind the bill already ended in a DUI conviction, so existing law works.

AB 2510.quote: Last year, I vetoed a substantially similar bill because it resulted in ongoing costs that were not accounted for in the budget. That is still the case this year
AB 2510.reason: He vetoed a substantially similar bill last year because it created ongoing costs that were not accounted for in the budget, and that is still true this year.

AB 2526.quote: this bill takes the wrong approach by expanding eligibility based on a determination by an IEP team — an imprecise measure of the cost and intensity of a student's education needs
AB 2526.reason: Special education funding rose 43% this budget ($2.4 billion ongoing, including $40 million more for low-incidence disabilities), but keying eligibility to an IEP team determination is an imprecise proxy for the cost and intensity of a student's needs, risks creating the wrong fiscal incentives, and could dilute funding for students who are already eligible.

AB 2543.quote: would divert the OES from core public safety missions by assigning work more appropriately led by agencies with energy systems expertise
AB 2543.reason: Supports keeping fuel and transportation running through emergencies, but a statewide assessment of this scale needs substantial new staffing and expertise and far more time than the bill allows, and it would pull the Office of Emergency Services off core public safety work that is better led by energy agencies such as the Energy Commission.

AB 255.quote: Establishing a separate certification and oversight process wrongly suggests incompatibility with Housing First, while imposing fees that would not cover implementation costs
AB 255.reason: California can already fund recovery housing inside the Housing First framework, so a separate certification and oversight category would be duplicative, would wrongly suggest recovery housing is incompatible with Housing First, and would charge fees that would not cover the cost of running it.

AB 2551.quote: it is unnecessary to require an additional forum outside these established processes
AB 2551.reason: Unnecessary: CSU and UC boards already hold regularly scheduled public meetings where the campus community can speak, and both systems have established channels between student associations and administrators, so mandating an extra forum adds nothing.

AB 2565.quote: guidance is already underway to address the concerns driving this legislation, making this bill unnecessary
AB 2565.reason: Supports clear guidance and enforcement for Medi-Cal plans on pharmacist services, but the department is already handling it: initial guidance went out in September 2025 and a comprehensive all-plan letter is coming, all within existing responsibilities that need no new statutory direction.

AB 2571.quote: this bill would result in millions of dollars in ongoing, annual costs related to FQHC reimbursement, as well as millions in one-time costs to implement the required system changes
AB 2571.reason: Wants better access to advanced pharmacist services, but setting Medi-Cal rates at 85% of the physician fee schedule would cost millions of dollars a year in ongoing FQHC reimbursement plus millions more in one-time system changes, none of it in this year's budget.

AB 2575.quote: linking anti-retaliation protections to a scope-of-practice determination puts the Labor Commissioner in the position of adjudicating the standard of care for patients
AB 2575.reason: Commends the goal of protecting clinicians' judgment against AI decision-support tools, but says the anti-retaliation language only bans action taken solely because of an override (a higher bar than other retaliation laws) and would make the Labor Commissioner decide questions of medical standard of care and scope of practice it has no expertise to judge.

AB 2588.quote: This bill would create a temporary appointment process outside this standard vetting framework, raising accountability and oversight concerns
AB 2588.reason: Shares the goal of keeping district agricultural association boards functional, but letting a board temporarily appoint its own director when the Governor has not filled a vacancy bypasses the standard vetting process and raises accountability and oversight concerns for decisions about state property.

AB 2593.quote: this bill may directly conflict with the court-ordered healthcare system established under Plata v. Newsom and may cause challenges with the federal courts
AB 2593.reason: Well intended, but the bill could conflict with the court-ordered prison health system under Plata v. Newsom and risk backsliding on returning health care to CDCR. It is also not clearly limited to state-employed providers, so supervisors might fear liability for questioning outside specialists' recommendations even when that review protects patients.

AB 2635.quote: this bill duplicates existing state and local air district programs
AB 2635.reason: Shares the goal of moving small off-road equipment to zero-emission, but the voucher program duplicates existing state and air district programs — $30 million already bought nearly 30,000 pieces of zero-emission landscape equipment and the market is now widely available.

AB 264.quote: this bill would result in General Fund ongoing costs in the millions of dollars annually and should be considered as part of the annual budget process
AB 264.reason: Supports expanding college fee waivers for veterans' dependents, but the change would cost the General Fund millions of dollars a year on an ongoing basis and should be weighed against other priorities in the annual budget process.

AB 265.quote: an unfunded grant program is of little use to small businesses and nonprofits without dedicated resources
AB 265.reason: He signed $2.5 billion in disaster relief two weeks after the LA wildfires and the state has administered over $3 billion in federal small business aid; an unfunded grant program is of little use without resources provided through the budget.

AB 2656.quote: this measure would impose redundant administrative layers on public agencies and slow the deployment of even the most innocuous tools
AB 2656.reason: Agrees workers should hear about new technology that affects them, but a 45-day notice before any generative AI use adds redundant administrative layers and would slow even innocuous tools; he says the issue is better handled through collective bargaining, where each workplace can tailor the rules.

AB 2717.quote: Failure to maintain effective control of outdoor advertising could jeopardize 10% of the state's federal highway funding
AB 2717.reason: Arena advertising revenue has local benefits, but he vetoed a similar bill in 2022 after the Federal Highway Administration said existing arena billboards did not comply with federal law; those risks remain and failing to control outdoor advertising could cost up to $580 million a year — 10% of the state's federal highway money.

AB 2721.quote: this bill introduces considerable consumer privacy and public safety concerns by compelling hotel operators to disclose this guest information not just to their employees, but to the public
AB 2721.reason: Calls the federal conduct abhorrent and points to SB 294 (2025) and expanded know-your-rights resources, but requiring hotels to disclose federal officers' presence to the public — not just employees — raises guest-privacy conflicts with state law and could provoke demonstrations that endanger workers and guests.

AB 2739.quote: by creating a permanent program without identifying a sustainable, ongoing funding source, this bill — as well as SB 1125 — misses the mark
AB 2739.reason: Water affordability is a priority and he appreciates the intent, but the bill creates a permanent program without a sustainable ongoing funding source (same criticism as SB 1125) and should come back next year as part of the budget process.

AB 2770.quote: I am concerned that piecemeal measures, like this bill, could undermine those values
AB 2770.reason: Supports returning ancestral land and points to co-management covering more than half of State Parks land and over 100,000 acres returned, but that work should be done systemically through transparent, fair processes; piecemeal land transfers like this one could undermine those values.

AB 306.quote: Allowing the same issues to be presented to the Building Standards Commission without specifying which agency has final authority could result in duplicative proceedings, inconsistent interpretations, and project delays
AB 306.reason: Last year's budget already adopted an earlier version's ideas (pausing new residential building standards to mid-2031), but the bill never explains how the commission's new appeals pathway interacts with the Energy Commission, Historical Building Safety Board, and State Fire Marshal, risking duplicative proceedings, inconsistent rulings, and housing delays — plus significant unfunded ongoing costs.

AB 353.quote: it would compromise the Public Advocates Office's (Office) role as a robust advocate before the CPUC
AB 353.reason: Wants more CPUC oversight, but the bill would compromise the Public Advocates Office by giving agency staff access to its internal deliberations, work product, and litigation strategy, undermining its independence — and a reorganization of this scale would cost tens of millions of dollars not in this year's budget.

AB 374.quote: the associated costs of implementation are estimated at tens of millions of dollars and are not accounted for in the state budget
AB 374.reason: The goal is laudable but implementation is estimated at tens of millions of dollars not in the state budget; he urged sponsors to work with school employers on a less costly way to get classified employees timely wage and leave information.

AB 393.quote: this measure circumvents the collective bargaining process and limits the ability of these departments to deliver critical services
AB 393.reason: Supports reducing reliance on contractors, but requiring a cost comparison before any personal services contract circumvents collective bargaining and limits the departments' ability to deliver critical services; it belongs in the budget and labor negotiations.

AB 399.quote: this bill creates a new, unfunded program
AB 399.reason: California has already invested about $9.6 billion in nature-based climate solutions between 2020 and 2024 and has carbon-removal targets from AB 1757; this would add a new, unfunded blue-carbon program on top of that during a tight budget year.

AB 400.quote: POST has provided guidelines regarding the use of police canines since 1991
AB 400.reason: Unnecessary: POST has issued police-canine guidelines since 1991 and just refreshed them after convening urban and rural agencies, Fish and Wildlife, CHP and State Parks, and its Use of Force guidelines already direct officers to act fairly and without bias.

AB 432.quote: This bill's expansive coverage mandate, in conjunction with a prohibition on UM, is too far-reaching
AB 432.reason: He vetoed a substantially similar bill last year: an expansive menopause coverage mandate combined with a ban on utilization management is too far-reaching and, with undefined terms, raises cost and implementation concerns amid double-digit premium increases. He directed CHHS to bring options in next year's budget.

AB 44.quote: this bill does not align with the California Public Utility Commission's Resource Adequacy framework
AB 44.reason: Would have the Energy Commission publish new electric load-forecast adjustment methodologies, but those methods would not line up with the CPUC's Resource Adequacy framework, so they would not improve grid-reliability planning and could create uncertainty in resource planning and procurement.

AB 449.quote: it will result in General Fund cost pressures to fund the campaigns and working group
AB 449.reason: Shares the commitment to fighting hate and points to Stop the Hate (over $100 million in grants), the Commission on the State of Hate, and the California vs. Hate hotline, but the new statewide and regional ad campaigns would create General Fund cost pressure outside the budget.

AB 464.quote: the bill's expanded tolling and claims provisions could expose the state to substantial and uncertain future liability without opportunity for the state to meaningfully investigate or rebut
AB 464.reason: Condemns sexual assault of incarcerated people and urges the Legislature to bring back the bill's monitoring, notification, reporting, and transfer provisions, but the expanded tolling plus exemption from the claims presentation requirement would expose the state to large, uncertain liability in cases where evidence and reliable witness memories are long gone.

AB 474.quote: By exempting nonprofit home-sharing programs from long-standing FEHA protections, the bill risks creating inconsistencies in California’s fair housing framework and causing legal uncertainty
AB 474.reason: A blanket exemption from the Fair Employment and Housing Act would create inconsistencies and legal uncertainty in California's fair-housing framework, and excluding home-sharing income only for state programs would clash with federal benefit rules and add administrative cost.

AB 512.quote: this bill's significantly shortened deadlines may inadvertently increase the number of denials
AB 512.reason: He signed SB 306 for a holistic prior-authorization fix; sharply shortened decision deadlines could increase denials and force plans to decide on incomplete information, so SB 306's more balanced approach should play out first.

AB 524.quote: recent budget action by the Legislature did not explicitly appropriate funding to support this program and there is no sustained funding
AB 524.reason: The farmland-access program could draw on Proposition 4 money, but the Legislature never actually appropriated funding for it and there is no sustained funding for its ongoing costs, so it fails the test of staying within the enacted budget.

AB 527.quote: the increased fees caused by this bill could disincentivize geothermal development in California
AB 527.reason: Supports geothermal as clean baseload power, but the bill would delay regulations already in process and force the division to raise operator fees substantially, which could disincentivize development more than the CEQA exemption helps; AB 1359's targeted reforms should be evaluated first.

AB 539.quote: this bill would apply prior authorizations too broadly, limiting health plans' ability to reassess medical necessity as a member's condition changes
AB 539.reason: Appreciates the goal of cutting administrative burden, but locking in prior authorizations for a year applies them too broadly and stops plans from reassessing medical necessity as a patient's condition changes, risking overutilization, inappropriate continuation of services, and conflict with clinical guidelines.

AB 546.quote: a mandate to cover air purifiers sets a precedent that goes beyond coverage for basic health care services
AB 546.reason: Sympathetic to wildfire victims needing clean air, but singling out HEPA purifiers for asthma and COPD could create disparities for people with other conditions, and covering air purifiers sets a precedent beyond basic health care services.

AB 554.quote: By exceeding the cost-sharing provisions under the ACA, this bill would result in increased costs to health plans
AB 554.reason: Supports affordable HIV prevention and codified the 2025 USPSTF no-cost preventive services in this budget, but going beyond ACA cost-sharing rules raises plan costs that pass to consumers — hard to justify amid double-digit premium increases.

AB 57.quote: creating an ancestry-based set-aside presents legal risks and could jeopardize CalHFA's access to federal mortgage markets
AB 57.reason: An ancestry-based set-aside carries legal risk and could jeopardize CalHFA's access to federal mortgage markets; the upcoming Dream for All round instead reserves 10% for borrowers in Qualified Census Tracts, advancing the same equity goals with less legal exposure.

AB 574.quote: It would be premature to establish limitations on the use of PA, as proposed by this bill, until SB 306 is fully implemented
AB 574.reason: Prior authorization appropriately applied contains costs and protects patients, and SB 306 already requires a data-driven list of services that should not need it; limiting PT prior authorization before SB 306 is implemented would be premature.

AB 605.quote: diverting these specialized inspectors to support the task force envisioned by this bill — without any identified resources — will diminish their ability to focus on holding refineries accountable
AB 605.reason: Supports planning for workers displaced by refinery closures, but the task force would be staffed by the Division of Occupational Safety and Health inspectors who enforce process-safety standards at refineries and chemical plants; diverting them without new resources could weaken oversight and put refinery workers at greater risk.

AB 615.quote: this bill is largely duplicative of existing requirements and mandates a new procedural requirement that risks delaying critical clean energy projects
AB 615.reason: Largely duplicative: SB 38 already requires battery storage owners to build emergency response plans with local agencies and comply with the latest NFPA standards, and the new procedural step risks delaying clean energy permits without adding safety.

AB 62.quote: CRD lacks the crucial expertise and immense resources required to successfully implement this bill
AB 62.reason: The Civil Rights Department is a prosecutorial agency without the expertise or resources to build a whole adjudicatory structure (including administrative law judges) for complex, evidence-heavy property disputes; the burden would undercut its core civil rights mission.

AB 620.quote: I encouraged rental vehicle companies to work with CARB to explore the environmental and economic benefits of MD/HD ZEV rentals through existing regulatory processes
AB 620.reason: He has pushed zero-emission trucks through executive orders and CARB's Advanced Clean Fleets rule; last year he urged rental companies to work with CARB through existing regulatory processes to explore medium- and heavy-duty zero-emission rentals, and continues to encourage that rather than legislating it.

AB 632.quote: I am concerned about expanding local authority to place liens on private property
AB 632.reason: Recognizes the difficulty of enforcing against illegal cannabis grows (and signed AB 1684 to strengthen local penalties), but expanding local authority to place liens on private property upsets the balance between homeowner due process and nuisance abatement; existing law strikes it right.

AB 650.quote: this bill would inappropriately shift responsibility for preparing housing elements from local jurisdictions to HCD
AB 650.reason: Would shift the job of writing housing elements from local jurisdictions to HCD; technical assistance is no substitute for local planning responsibility, and the change would add at least $11 million in new annual costs.

AB 664.quote: This bill contains a provision that states it will not go into effect, even with my signature, if AB 2694 and SB 960 become law. To avoid confusion, I am vetoing this bill
AB 664.reason: He signed AB 2694 and SB 960 to create a statewide framework for community college bachelor's degrees, and this bill says it would not take effect if those become law. He vetoed it to avoid confusion and urged the district to use the new statewide option instead.

AB 682.quote: This bill creates duplicative and conflicting health plan reporting requirements
AB 682.reason: He signed SB 306, which already requires plans and insurers to report prior-authorization data to the regulators; this bill's added reporting is duplicative and conflicting, risking confusion that could hinder the transparency it seeks.

AB 689.quote: this bill would create a new, unfunded grant program
AB 689.reason: Creating a Child Welfare Disaster Response Fund and program would establish a new, unfunded grant program with no identified funding source, producing significant ongoing General Fund cost pressure each year.

AB 695.quote: this proposal only benefits immigrant students who voluntarily or involuntarily depart the U.S ... raising significant constitutional concerns
AB 695.reason: Proud of the state's protections for immigrant students, but as drafted the tuition exemption benefits only students who departed the U.S. and not residents of other states, raising significant constitutional concerns.

AB 696.quote: would be uncoordinated with the work being done through the Collaborative and it is largely duplicative
AB 696.reason: He already created the California Battery Safety Collaborative, which includes the State Fire Marshal; a new advisory group would be uncoordinated and largely duplicate the Lithium Ion Car Battery Recycling Advisory Group's completed work. He directed the Collaborative to expand to mobile battery storage.

AB 699.quote: I am concerned that this bill, as drafted, will reduce transparency for local tax and bond measures
AB 699.reason: Letting a local elections official point voters to the county voter guide instead of printing the required tax-rate information on the ballot label would, as drafted, reduce transparency for local tax and bond measures.

AB 7.quote: These institutions already have the authority to determine whether to provide admissions preferences like this one, and accordingly, this bill is unnecessary
AB 7.reason: Unnecessary: public and private colleges already have the authority to decide whether to give an admissions preference to descendants of slavery, so he encouraged institutions to consider it themselves.

AB 713.quote: the federal courts must resolve the legality of the novel legal theory behind this legislation before we proceed
AB 713.reason: He vetoed a nearly identical bill two years ago and his concerns have grown: barring public universities from requiring federal work authorization could expose state employees to criminal and civil liability, so the novel legal theory should be settled in federal court (via declaratory relief) first.

AB 734.quote: the risks associated with this divulgence of information and the added procedural requirement of a CDFW determination on whether to divulge such information, if found harmful, are unnecessary
AB 734.reason: Detailed biological-resource maps are kept at limited resolution under Fish and Wildlife data rules precisely to protect sensitive species from poaching, collection and habitat disturbance; releasing them would add risk and an extra agency determination without producing new protections.

AB 738.quote: Codifying the broad exemption in this bill would permanently nullify these positive outcomes for homeowners
AB 738.reason: The solar requirement has cut homeowner energy costs for five years; a broad statutory exemption for disaster rebuilds would permanently nullify those benefits and ignore local rebuilding differences. His targeted executive order for the LA fires, which kept solar-ready requirements, is the balanced approach to retain.

AB 740.quote: this bill results in costs to the CEC's primary operating fund, which is currently facing an ongoing structural deficit
AB 740.reason: Supports virtual power plants and distributed resources, but requiring a deployment plan and annual utility load-shift reports would draw on the Energy Commission's primary operating fund, which already faces an ongoing structural deficit.

AB 742.quote: I believe more data is needed on the effectiveness and consequences of expedited licensure
AB 742.reason: As more applicants qualify for expedited licensure the benefit of mandated prioritization diminishes and other applicants are hurt, and staffing the expedited queue could raise licensing fees. He vetoed two similar bills last year and wants data first.

AB 76.quote: it is premature to alter this exemption before the task force completes its evaluation
AB 76.reason: Supports a University Innovation District in Chula Vista (and signed AB 662's task force), but excluding student, faculty, and staff housing from affordability calculations would erode a Surplus Land Act framework that has produced 34,000 homes including 21,500 affordable ones — and the task force has not finished its work.

AB 760.quote: I stated that future measures, like this bill, should be included in the annual budget process, given the General Fund implications
AB 760.reason: Wholeheartedly supports excluding Garden Grove chemical-leak settlement payments from state tax, and signed similar wildfire exclusions in 2022, but said then — and applied to AB 1973 and SB 542 in 2024 — that measures with General Fund implications should go through the annual budget process.

AB 766.quote: the bill's timelines for reporting on strategic plans, along with the additional information entities must include in their plan and uncertainty around which entities are required to comply, are unworkable
AB 766.reason: He signed EO N-16-22 and created the Racial Equity Commission, but the bill's reporting deadlines, required plan contents, and unclear list of covered entities are unworkable, and expanding reporting across all entities under his purview carries costs not in the budget agreement.

AB 788.quote: creating a new parallel Division within the CDCR to administer only two institutions is not advised
AB 788.reason: Agrees incarcerated women need a different approach, but a separate division to run only two institutions would bloat CDCR's administration, duplicate existing work, and create organizational dysfunction — especially after the 2025 realignment grouped both women's institutions under one regional associate director — and it would add costs outside the budget.

AB 797.quote: would result in significant, ongoing General Fund impacts in the tens of millions of dollars not included in the 2025 Budget Act
AB 797.reason: Wholeheartedly supports fair redevelopment of disaster-damaged homes, but running the proposed IBank securities program would create significant ongoing General Fund costs in the tens of millions of dollars not included in the 2025 Budget Act.

AB 81.quote: this bill would lead to significant fiscal costs outside of the budget
AB 81.reason: Supports research on women veterans' mental health, but the study and report would create significant costs outside the budget — the same reason he vetoed a similar measure last year, when he urged securing funding through the budget process.

AB 823.quote: ban specific ingredients, such as glitter, which may incidentally result in a prohibition on biodegradable or natural alternatives
AB 823.reason: Supports fighting microplastics, but banning specific ingredients such as glitter could incidentally prohibit biodegradable or natural alternatives.

AB 830.quote: Creating a statutory exception for one utility in a single county undermines fiscal discipline and creates inequities across California
AB 830.reason: Recognizes the burden of relocation costs, but shifting them to the state for one Mendocino County utility district contradicts the longstanding rule that permittees pay, and a one-off statutory exception undermines fiscal discipline and creates inequities across California.

AB 833.quote: there is no statutory barrier to expanding program sponsorship for teachers from other countries
AB 833.reason: Unnecessary: no statutory barrier prevents expanding teacher-exchange sponsorship (federal law does not require a single exclusive sponsor), and the author's goal of filling educator shortages is contrary to the program's purpose of cross-cultural understanding and short-term professional growth.

AB 843.quote: California already has comprehensive language assistance laws, including a detailed all-encompassing language assistance program regulation, that fulfills the intent of this bill
AB 843.reason: Unnecessary: California already has a comprehensive language-assistance regulation that fulfills the bill's intent, so copying federal language-access rules into state law would duplicate requirements, create confusion, and add costs to the health care system.

AB 86.quote: Proposals like AB 86 should only be considered after this study is complete and changes to the process are adopted
AB 86.reason: The Budget Act of 2025 already funded a Curriculum Guidance Study of how the state adopts curriculum guidance; new instructional-materials mandates should wait until that study is finished, and local school boards keep the authority to select materials in the meantime.

AB 880.quote: concerned that the policy would allocate a significant amount of grant funding toward indirect costs, rather than project implementation and outcomes for California
AB 880.reason: Values nonprofit partners, but has vetoed nearly identical bills before because reimbursing indirect costs shifts significant grant money away from project delivery and outcomes; the cost pressure on the state remains the concern.

AB 915.quote: it is imperative that we do so with safety at the forefront
AB 915.reason: Exempting compressed-air energy-storage water facilities from state dam-safety oversight and fees would put safety second; oversight costs must be recovered from project developers so agencies can enforce the safety requirements.

AB 917.quote: eliminates many of the flexibilities established for small school districts in light of the unique circumstances
AB 917.reason: Laudable intent, but granting permanent status after two years in small districts strips away flexibilities built for their unique circumstances and could hurt students; permanency can be handled in collective bargaining. Limiting regional occupational programs' nimbleness also cuts against aligning education with workforce demand.

AB 93.quote: I am reluctant to impose rigid reporting requirements about operational details on this sector
AB 93.reason: California wants to support data center growth as AI demand explodes; he is reluctant to impose rigid operational reporting on the sector without understanding the full impact on businesses and their customers.

AB 963.quote: this bill creates redundant processes that could undermine other enforcement priorities
AB 963.reason: Agrees prevailing wage laws need compliance, but the bill creates redundant record-request processes when parties can already request payroll records and the public can access them; it would also generate significant new workload for a Labor Commissioner's Office with limited capacity.

AB 975.quote: CDFW would still be required to develop individualized fish and wildlife resource protections for exempt projects, creating unknown but potentially significant General Fund cost pressures
AB 975.reason: Fish and Wildlife would still have to write individualized fish and wildlife protections for the exempt bridge and culvert projects, and because the number and scope of qualifying projects is unknown the exemption could create significant, unbudgeted General Fund cost pressure.

AB 986.quote: this language encompasses comparable events such as landslides, mudslides, and related geologic hazards without the need for further statutory amendment
AB 986.reason: Unnecessary: the Emergency Services Act already lets the Governor proclaim a State of Emergency for 'conditions of disaster or extreme peril,' which covers landslides, mudslides and related geologic hazards; enumerating landslides would add no power and could imply that unlisted events are ineligible.

SB 1029.quote: this bill divides responsibility between two state agencies without establishing a clear process for verifying ownership, resolving claims, or making final eligibility determinations
SB 1029.reason: Supports returning excess lien-sale proceeds to vehicle owners, but the bill splits responsibility between DMV and the Controller with no clear process for verifying ownership or resolving claims, and would add administrative costs to the Motor Vehicle Account without showing more money would reach owners.

SB 1037.quote: This bill approach is premature, but the intention to address rising healthcare costs could not be more timely
SB 1037.reason: Premature: the Office of Health Care Affortability's statewide cost-growth target only took effect in 2024 and there has not been enough time to enforce it or judge its impact. He instead directed DMHC and OHCA (and asked CDI) to weigh plans' compliance with the cost target during premium rate review under existing law.

SB 1057.quote: this bill unacceptably and unavoidably weakens Medicare and Medi-Cal program integrity by requiring the state to certify federally ineligible individuals
SB 1057.reason: Online continuing education for nurse assistants is welcome, but the criminal-record changes would strip the department of routine enforcement tools (no action until conviction and appeals are exhausted, none on dismissed convictions), and requiring certification of federally ineligible individuals weakens Medicare and Medi-Cal program integrity, jeopardizes facility funding, and endangers patients.

SB 1059.quote: the recordkeeping requirements for ETP contracts would be more appropriately addressed under existing regulatory authority
SB 1059.reason: Supports modernizing the Employment Training Panel, but recordkeeping standards for its contracts are better set through the panel's existing regulatory authority, where employers and stakeholders can comment and costs can be weighed. He directed the panel to consider rules matching the bill's goals.

SB 1064.quote: Reduced testing would allow malfunctioning emissions systems to go undetected for extended periods, worsening air quality
SB 1064.reason: Clean Truck Check is critical to cutting truck emissions; halving testing frequency would let malfunctioning emissions systems go undetected, worsening air along freight corridors. With California already facing a 165-ton-per-day NOx deficit, weakening it risks federal attainment obligations and tens of billions in transportation funding — and flexible compliance options already exist.

SB 1077.quote: this bill imposes requirements that CDSS simply cannot implement, while also limiting the state's flexibility to stay nimble
SB 1077.reason: After last fall's 43-day federal shutdown California ran Operation Feed California — Service Corps and National Guard at food banks plus roughly $80 million in emergency state funding — but the mandated webpage, communications plan, and shutdown benefit-issuance mechanism are things the department cannot implement, much of the required information simply does not exist during a shutdown, and the rules would limit the state's flexibility.

SB 11.quote: it is unclear whether a warning would be sufficient to dissuade wrongdoers from using AI to impersonate others
SB 11.reason: Shares the concern about AI impersonation, but the bill requires every generative tool to link a liability disclosure at every prompt input on pain of significant civil liability, and it is unclear a warning would actually deter wrongdoers.

SB 1105.quote: it would be unwise to jeopardize this apparatus for the purpose of restating existing protections in law
SB 1105.reason: State law already bars racial profiling; forcing renegotiation of existing interagency agreements would disrupt critical public safety work — drug and human trafficking, counterterrorism, cybersecurity, LA28 preparations, the Joint Terrorism Task Force — an unacceptable price for restating protections already in law.

SB 1125.quote: by creating a permanent program without identifying a sustainable, ongoing funding source, this bill — as well as AB 2739 — misses the mark
SB 1125.reason: Water affordability is a top priority and the intent is appreciated, but a permanent direct bill-assistance program with no sustainable ongoing funding source misses the mark (same criticism as AB 2739) and should be revisited in the budget process.

SB 1130.quote: This measure defines several terms too broadly or imprecisely
SB 1130.reason: Supports responding to invasive recording by camera-equipped wearables, but the bill defines several terms too broadly or imprecisely (its 'wearable recording device' could reach smartwatches), and existing law already criminalizes recording someone where they have a reasonable expectation of privacy.

SB 1173.quote: I do not support upsetting the balance struck by the California Supreme Court in the Birks decision
SB 1173.reason: The California Supreme Court rejected the lesser-related offense rule in People v. Birks (1998) as unfair to the prosecution, promoting inaccurate fact-finding, and possibly violating separation of powers; those concerns are still valid and he will not upset that balance.

SB 1180.quote: this bill risks complicating implementation of both the Act and the Fund
SB 1180.reason: Commends the circular-economy goal, but the administration is still doing the foundational work of implementing the plastic producer responsibility act; much of what the bill requires is already underway and this would risk complicating implementation of both the act and the fund.

SB 1194.quote: this bill, which creates an unfunded program on top of this work, is duplicative and unnecessary
SB 1194.reason: This year's budget doubled immigration legal-services funding to nearly $150 million, including $7.5 million for the very Immigration Legal Fellowship Project this bill creates plus $34.3 million to nonprofits, so the bill adds an unfunded, duplicative program on top of funded work.

SB 1238.quote: Establishing a duty owed to both the association and its individual members could create conflicting obligations
SB 1238.reason: Making an HOA managing agent owe a duty of care to both the association and individual members creates conflicting obligations when interests diverge, inviting litigation homeowners would pay for, and it is unclear how the new duty interacts with existing common-law obligations. Other provisions overlap existing reserve-planning and records rules.

SB 1240.quote: the establishment and continued operation of this new office would result in millions of dollars of costs outside of the budget process
SB 1240.reason: Appreciates the goal of a dedicated office for nonprofit policy, but creating and running a new Office of Nonprofit Empowerment and fund would cost millions of dollars outside the budget process.

SB 1272.quote: This measure would tie their hands with a one-size-fits-all approach, leading to increased local government costs and unnecessary delays
SB 1272.reason: Sympathetic to new owners inheriting undisclosed code problems, but local officials need discretion in code enforcement; a one-size-fits-all minimum six-month (plus six-month) correction period would tie their hands and raise local costs and delays.

SB 1340.quote: this bill's proposed manual review and collection requirement, when applied across all agencies that execute procurement contracts, would result in additional spending in the tens of millions of dollars annually
SB 1340.reason: Supports consistent statewide reporting on small business contracting, but manually reviewing and collecting contract data across every procuring agency would cost tens of millions of dollars a year, outside the budget.

SB 224.quote: I am satisfied with DWR's response to this audit ... As a result, this bill is unnecessary
SB 224.reason: Unnecessary: the State Auditor found no unnecessary water release, DWR has already implemented the auditor's recommendations including additional climate change modeling, and its June report to the auditor satisfied the Governor.

SB 24.quote: this bill contains a significant clerical error related to the definition of "political influence activity," where two provisions directly contradict one another
